architecture.pattern: Single-purpose monitoring plane: one Spring Boot Admin (SBA) server on a fixed port, self-secured by Spring Security, self-registering into Consul; no business logic, no persistence, no inbound API of its own.
evidence: admin-service module contains exactly 2 .java files, 1 .yml, 1 pom.xml (+ Maven wrapper + .iml); no src/test, no Dockerfile

businessModules.name: monitoring-plane

integrations.name: Spring Boot Admin Server

integrations.purpose: The whole service - SBA server UI + registration API + instance aggregation.
integrations.complianceHint: Version is inherited from the root pom property ${spring-boot-admin.version}; the brief/Phase 3 record it as 2.7.7. Do not pin a version locally - bump the parent property instead.

integrations.name: Spring Boot Admin login UI (legacy)
integrations.purpose: Adds a pre-built standalone login page artifact from the SBA 1.x UI line. NO code in this module imports or references it - the only two classes are AdminServiceApplication and WebSecurityConfig, and WebSecurityConfig.java:39 points formLogin at the SBA 2.x server's own /login page.
integrations.complianceHint: Declared-but-unreferenced dependency, explicitly versioned outside the BOM. Carries a second UI jar alongside the 2.x server UI; candidate for removal after a build check. Brief records the property value as 1.5.7.

integrations.name: HashiCorp Consul service discovery
integrations.purpose: Registers admin-service itself in Consul as service id 'admin-service' (spring.application.name) and puts a DiscoveryClient on the classpath - the only registration mechanism available to the SBA server here.
integrations.complianceHint: host/port are hardcoded localhost:8500 with no spring.cloud.consul.token (ACL) and no TLS property. register-health-check: false means Consul never health-checks the admin UI.

integrations.name: Spring Security (servlet)
integrations.purpose: Protects the SBA UI: form login + HTTP Basic + remember-me + cookie CSRF repository.
integrations.complianceHint: One in-memory user from committed YAML (see gaps/risk). No roles, no OAuth2/OIDC/LDAP, no session concurrency control.

integrations.name: spring-boot-starter-web (Tomcat/MVC)
integrations.purpose: Servlet container serving the SBA UI on :5555.
integrations.complianceHint: No server.address set -> binds all interfaces. No spring-boot-starter-actuator and no spring-boot-starter-test dependency in this module.

containers.note: No Dockerfile / Containerfile / .dockerignore anywhere under admin-service/ (glob of admin-service/** returned 9 files: pom.xml, admin-service.iml, mvnw, mvnw.cmd, .mvn/wrapper/maven-wrapper.{properties,jar}, application.yml, 2 .java files). Phase 3 records Dockerfiles only for person-service and user-service, so this service is run with java -jar / mvn spring-boot:run.

orchestration.note: No Kubernetes manifests, Helm chart, kustomization or Terraform/OpenTofu file under admin-service/. Instances are addressed exclusively through Consul service discovery (service id = spring.application.name = admin-service).

pipelines.note: No pipeline file in this component: no .github/, no .gitlab-ci.yml, no Jenkinsfile, no Azure/GitHub workflow, no build script. Nothing in the module builds, tests, scans or deploys it automatically.

environments: default profile ONLY - no spring.profiles.active and no application-<profile>.yml under admin-service/src/main/resources/ (single file: application.yml). No bootstrap.yml.

server.port: 5555 - verified at admin-service/src/main/resources/application.yml:1-2. Fixed port, unlike person-service/user-service/notification-service, which set server.port: 0 (out-of-scope note from Phase 3).
No server.address / management.server.address / server.servlet.context-path set -> Tomcat binds 0.0.0.0:5555 and the SBA UI is served at '/'.

Consul: spring.cloud.consul.host: localhost, spring.cloud.consul.port: 8500 (application.yml:12-14); spring.cloud.consul.discovery.register-health-check: false (application.yml:15-16). No instance-id, hostname, port, tags, scheme or ACL token override -> all Consul discovery defaults.
spring.application.name: admin-service (application.yml:9) is the Consul service id and the only identity this module publishes.
Environment NAMES present in this module: none. The tokens dev / prod / staging / test / qa / local do not occur in any file under admin-service/.
Deploy target is implied, never declared: localhost development machine (Consul on localhost:8500) with a relative log path logs/admin-service.log.
Build toolchain pinned per-module: Maven 3.8.6 via Maven Wrapper 3.1.0 (admin-service/.mvn/wrapper/maven-wrapper.properties:1-2).
observability: @EnableAdminServer on pro.algotrade.adminservice.AdminServiceApplication (AdminServiceApplication.java:7, import line 3 de.codecentric.boot.admin.server.config.EnableAdminServer) - the only annotation on the class besides @SpringBootApplication.

Server dependency: de.codecentric:spring-boot-admin-starter-server, versionless in admin-service/pom.xml:28-31, managed by the spring-boot-admin-dependencies BOM import at pom.xml:55-61 keyed on ${spring-boot-admin.version}.

de.codecentric:spring-boot-admin-server-ui-login:${spring-boot-admin-ui.version} (pom.xml:33-37) - the SBA 1.x standalone login-page jar. NOT wired: no class in this module references it and formLogin uses the SBA 2.x built-in /login (WebSecurityConfig.java:39). Verdict: declared-but-unwired, likely 1.x-era residue.

Security gate on the UI: WebSecurityConfig.java:35-49 - permitAll for <ctx>/assets/** and <ctx>/login; anyRequest().authenticated(); formLogin(loginPage <ctx>/login, redirectTo param) + logout <ctx>/logout + httpBasic + CSRF(CookieCsrfTokenRepository.withHttpOnlyFalse, ignoring POST /instances, DELETE /instances/*, /actuator/**) + rememberMe(key=UUID.randomUUID(), 60s).

Session model: default servlet container HTTP session. No sessionManagement(), no maximumSessions, no session fixation protection override, no OAuth2 resource-server config, no CORS configuration anywhere in the module.

Registration model assumed by THIS module: discovery-based via Consul. It sets zero active spring.boot.admin.* property - the only spring.boot.admin.client.* keys present (url/username/password/instance.metadata.user.*) are commented out at application.yml:24-35, so admin-service does not self-register and holds NO credentials for protected instances. Property names actually read: server.port, spring.application.name, spring.cloud.consul.host, spring.cloud.consul.port, spring.cloud.consul.discovery.register-health-check, spring.security.user.name, spring.security.user.password, logging.*, plus spring.boot.admin.server.context-path consumed implicitly through the injected AdminServerProperties (WebSecurityConfig.java:20).

Actuator: this module consumes NO actuator endpoint of its own - spring-boot-starter-actuator is absent from admin-service/pom.xml, and the only management.* key (management.endpoints.web.exposure.include: "*") is commented out (application.yml:4-6). The endpoint set the SBA UI calls is a spring-boot-admin-starter-server library default, not configured here; the only module-level actuator artefact is the inert CSRF exemption for /actuator/** (WebSecurityConfig.java:48).

Logging: logging.file.name logs/admin-service.log (application.yml:39-40) - relative to the process CWD, plain-text, no pattern/layout or JSON encoder configured; rolling policy logback.rollingpolicy.max-file-size 10Mb, max-history 7 (application.yml:44-47); levels logging.level.org.hibernate.SQL debug and logging.level.org.hibernate.type.descriptor.sql trace (application.yml:41-43) - dead settings, no Hibernate in this module's dependency list.

Consul registration has NO health check (register-health-check: false, application.yml:16), so a crashed admin-service stays registered; and with no actuator dependency Consul has nothing to poll even if it were enabled.

crossComponentDependencies.note: Maven parent pro.algotrade:algo-trade-platform:1.0 (aggregator pom.xml). Supplies java.version, ${spring-cloud.version}, ${spring-boot-admin.version}, ${spring-boot-admin-ui.version} and spring-boot-starter-parent dependency management. Not followed - outside scope.

No sibling module is named, imported or URL-referenced anywhere in admin-service. Coupling is name-agnostic: any service that Consul knows about can appear in the UI. Sibling modules' own spring.boot.admin.client.url values are outside scope.

gaps: ${spring-boot-admin.version} and ${spring-boot-admin-ui.version} are resolved in the root pom.xml <properties>, which is outside this brief's scope; the values 2.7.7 / 1.5.7 used above come from the dispatch brief and Phase 3 notes, not from a file read here.

The concrete actuator endpoints each registered service exposes cannot be determined from admin-service - it declares no management.* keys of its own and sibling resource configuration is out of scope.
Whether sibling services push themselves to this UI through spring.boot.admin.client.url, or are only discovered through Consul, is decided entirely outside admin-service and was not read.

The runtime effect of putting spring-boot-admin-server-ui-login (1.x jar) on the same classpath as the 2.x SBA server UI cannot be verified without a build - this analysis is read-only and no Maven execution is permitted.

Whether :5555 is reachable beyond localhost in practice (reverse proxy, firewall, Docker network, ingress) is not expressible in this module - it has no container, orchestration or pipeline definition - so exposure is judged from configuration alone.

admin-service/mvnw (POSIX shell) and .mvn/wrapper/maven-wrapper.jar (binary) were not opened; the wrapper version comes from .mvn/wrapper/maven-wrapper.properties and mvnw.cmd's standard Apache header.
recommendations: Externalise spring.security.user.name / spring.security.user.password (application.yml:20-21) - they are plaintext literals in a committed file - and rotate them; source them from an env var or Consul KV.

Set server.address: 127.0.0.1 (or keep :5555 on a private network) unless the admin UI is deliberately reachable beyond the developer machine - nothing in this module restricts the bind address today.
Remove de.codecentric:spring-boot-admin-server-ui-login from pom.xml:33-37 after a build check - it is unreferenced by any class in this module.

Delete the two org.hibernate logging levels (application.yml:41-43) or move them to a non-default profile - they do nothing here and would emit SQL with bound parameters if a JPA starter were ever added.

Add spring-boot-starter-actuator and an explicit management.endpoints.web.exposure.include allowlist if admin-service should monitor itself, then re-enable the commented client block (application.yml:24-35); otherwise document that the monitoring plane is deliberately unmonitored.

Fix WebSecurityConfig.java:49 - rememberMe key UUID.randomUUID() invalidates every remember-me token on restart and tokenValiditySeconds(60) makes it useless; either set a stable key with a sane TTL or drop rememberMe.
Set spring.cloud.consul.discovery.register-health-check: true (application.yml:16) once actuator is present, so Consul can evict a dead admin UI.
Parameterise Consul host/port as ${CONSUL_HOST:localhost} / ${CONSUL_PORT:8500} and add a profile scheme - the module currently has exactly one environment (default).
